concept.title: Introduction to Excel, Workbook, Worksheet, Ribbon and Cells

images.title: Ribbon Interface, Cell Address, Formula Bar and Name Box

body: Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet application developed by Microsoft. It is used to organize, analyze, calculate, and visualize data efficiently.
Excel is widely used in schools, colleges, businesses, banks, hospitals, research organizations, and government offices for maintaining records and performing calculations.
A Workbook is an Excel file that can contain one or more Worksheets. The default file extension is .xlsx.
A Worksheet is a single spreadsheet page inside a workbook where data is entered and managed.
Rows run horizontally and are identified by numbers (1, 2, 3...). Columns run vertically and are identified by letters (A, B, C...).
A Cell is the intersection of a row and a column. Every cell has a unique address such as A1, B5, or C10.
The Ribbon is the command area at the top of Excel that contains tabs such as Home, Insert, Page Layout, Formulas, Data, Review, and View.
The Formula Bar displays the contents or formula of the selected cell.
The Name Box displays the address of the currently selected (active) cell.
The active cell is the currently selected cell where data can be entered or edited.
Excel automatically recalculates formulas whenever the data changes, making it an excellent tool for data analysis.
Keyboard shortcuts such as Ctrl+S (Save), Ctrl+C (Copy), Ctrl+V (Paste), Ctrl+Z (Undo), and Ctrl+B (Bold) improve productivity.

questions.question: What is Microsoft Excel primarily used for?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet application used for storing, organizing, analyzing, and calculating data.

questions.question: What is an Excel Workbook?
questions.explanation: A Workbook is an Excel file that contains one or more worksheets.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a valid cell address?
questions.explanation: A valid cell address is formed using the column letter followed by the row number.

questions.question: Rows in Excel are identified using:
questions.explanation: Rows are numbered 1, 2, 3, and so on.

questions.question: Columns in Excel are identified using:
questions.explanation: Columns are labeled A, B, C, D, and so on.

questions.question: What is the intersection of a row and a column called?
questions.explanation: The intersection of a row and column is called a Cell.

questions.question: Which Excel component displays formulas and cell contents?
questions.explanation: The Formula Bar displays the contents or formula of the active cell.

questions.question: Which component contains commands like Home, Insert, Formulas, and Data?
questions.explanation: The Ribbon organizes all Excel commands into different tabs.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut saves the current workbook?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + S saves the current workbook.

questions.question: The Name Box in Excel displays:
questions.explanation: The Name Box displays the address of the currently selected cell, such as A1 or C5.
